name: On GPUs in NVIDIA Confidential Computing mode, vLLM's V2 model runner serves silent garbage
symptom: On an H100 NVL in CC mode inside a TDX guest, vLLM 0.29.0 with the default V2 GPU model runner starts and serves, but every response is garbage - '!!!!!!!!' (token id 0 repeated) or '[][][][]'. No error or warning anywhere. The same model is correct under plain transformers on the same GPU, so it is easy to blame the GPU or the CC setup.
root_cause: The V2 runner feeds input_ids, positions and block tables to the GPU through UVA views of pinned host memory (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/buffer_utils.py -> UvaBuffer -> get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor -> torch.ops._C.get_cuda_view_from_cpu_tensor). Under GPU CC the device cannot access guest memory directly; all host/device traffic goes through the driver's encrypted bounce buffer, so those views are stale.
workaround: Set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 to fall back to the V1 runner, which produces correct output on the same setup.
notes: Diagnostic ordering that matters here: the same guest runs transformers, CuPy and plain torch correctly, so 'works under transformers' does NOT rule out the GPU or CC configuration. Test vLLM's runner version before suspecting hardware.
